title: Build a generic FIFO queue in Go using generics
description: Greenfield Go task: implement a generic Queue[T any] backed by a slice with Push, Pop (bool ok), Peek, Len, and IsEmpty methods. No concurrency required.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement Queue[T any] in queue.go.

type Queue[T any] struct { ... }

func NewQueue[T any]() *Queue[T]
func (q *Queue[T]) Push(v T)           // enqueue at back
func (q *Queue[T]) Pop() (T, bool)     // dequeue from front; zero + false if empty
func (q *Queue[T]) Peek() (T, bool)    // view front without removing; zero + false if empty
func (q *Queue[T]) Len() int
func (q *Queue[T]) IsEmpty() bool

All 5 tests in queue_test.go must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: Pop dequeues from front and returns (zero, false) when empty
Peek returns front without removing; (zero, false) when empty
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
